## Recommended direction: “freight evidence, treated like institutional records”

Use **deep evergreen and near-black ink, a restrained oxidized-copper accent, and fine matte texture**. Build depth through tonal surfaces and precise document presentation—not checkerboards, cream, glowing blobs, or decorative logistics photography.

Below, **verified** means documented by the studio responsible. The FreightClaimKit adaptations and hex values are my recommendations, not extracted brand specifications.

### Six primary-source references

| Reference / direct case-study URL | Verified color / material lesson | Suggested application to FreightClaimKit |
|---|---|---|
| **[Cohere — Pentagram](https://www.pentagram.com/work/cohere)** · Enterprise software | The palette explicitly combines **coniferous green, mushroom grey and volcanic black** with coral, quartz and blue. Pentagram describes gradient “atmospheres” as less visually dominant than its 3D cells or patterns; the identity extends to the website and dashboard. [web:42] | **Strongest color reference.** Borrow green/black with one warm accent. Omit the cells, tessellations and atmospheric gradients: the palette can carry the page without another decorative system. |
| **[Lendbridge — NEUE WORLD](https://www.neue.world/case-studies/lendbridge)** · Private lending | Documents **dominant deep forest green**, electric-mint accents, embossed stationery and reversed business cards. Its green-to-amber gradient belongs to asset-value illustrations—not a documented universal background texture. [web:22] | Borrow the **large, confident green surfaces** and quiet embossed-material cue. Replace electric mint with muted copper; skip pixel icons and wireframe assets. |
| **[Copper — KOTA](https://kota.co.uk/work/copper)** · Financial infrastructure | KOTA specifies **charcoal and white** for authority, supported by oxide, lilac, salmon and mint. Technical illustration and flexible grids are also part of the identity; the source does **not** document a grain treatment. [web:26] | Borrow charcoal contrast and an **oxide-like warm accent**, not the entire multicolor system or grids. Keep warmth concentrated on the primary action and a few editorial markers. |
| **[G.F Smith / Colorplan — Made Thought](https://www.madethought.com/work/gf-smith)** · Premium materials brand | The studio frames the work as a “tactile universe.” Its related **[Possibilities of Paper project](https://www.madethought.com/g-f-smith-presents-sonderegger)** specifically documents raster engraving, ink over foil and debossing in a physical print series. These are material references, not verified website-background effects. [web:43][web:44] | Translate **pigmented paper and shallow impression** into digital surfaces: fine monochrome grain and subtle inset edges. No beige paper, distressed parchment or literal butterfly imagery. |
| **[Dessia — Gemeos](https://www.gemeosagency.com/en/our-projects/dessia)** · Industrial engineering SaaS | The case study documents a blue/metallic redesign. Its explored **“AI & SaaS” direction** explicitly uses subtle metallic texture; another direction uses metallic greys, deep blues and a “cut edge” motif. The page presents multiple explorations, so those details should not all be treated as shipped features. [web:36] | Borrow **industrial precision**, not electric blue: a graphite inset surface or a single clipped edge around an evidence preview. Avoid chrome reflections and heavily brushed-metal effects. |
| **[PAXAFE — The Branx](https://thebranx.com/work/paxafe)** · Supply-chain risk SaaS | Explicitly uses **black backgrounds and industrial blue-grey**, with red-to-green serving risk communication. Golden road imagery and illustrative animation are documented separately; no fine-grain texture is specified. [web:32] | Closest category reference: distinguish **brand atmosphere from evidence status**. Use dark surfaces for authority; reserve red/green for actual exceptions and verified states. Replace scenic imagery with a legible claim packet. |

### Implementable palette

**Proposed FreightClaimKit tokens—not sampled reference colors.**

| Token | Hex | Application |
|---|---|---|
| Evergreen | `#102D28` | Main page background |
| Ink | `#081A17` | Navigation, hero recess, footer |
| Raised green | `#1A3B33` | Product frames and selected panels |
| Copper | `#D58C65` | Primary CTA and sparse emphasis; use ink-colored button text |
| Cool chalk | `#EDF3F0` | Main text and occasional document surface; explicitly not cream |
| Muted sage | `#B0C2BA` | Secondary copy on dark surfaces |
| Evergreen rule | `#34564B` | Dividers and component outlines |

### Background treatments to build

| Surface | Implementation recipe |
|---|---|
| **Matte evergreen field** | Solid evergreen with a locally generated, seamless monochrome noise tile at **approximately 1.5–2.5% opacity**. Keep the noise static and behind content—not over text or controls. It should register as material, not visible speckle. |
| **Recessed ink stage** | Place the hero evidence preview on an ink panel. Use one subdued top-edge highlight and a shallow inset shadow. Keep most of the surrounding surface empty; no nested decorative cards or ambient glow. |
| **Evidence-document contrast** | Show one sharply typeset cool-chalk claim summary against the dark field, with restrained stacking behind it. Use synthetic sample data, timestamps, attachment counts and provenance labels—not stock photos or fake dashboard decoration. |
| **Quiet section transitions** | Alternate evergreen and ink through clean full-width boundaries and generous spacing. Use occasional single rules, never repeating background lines, checkerboards or dot matrices. |

**First prototype:** ink navigation → evergreen hero → recessed evidence packet → evergreen workflow → ink closing CTA. Copper appears primarily on **“Build an evidence packet.”** The premium effect should survive with all texture disabled; texture is the finishing layer, not the concept.
